sources.entry: OpenScreen - Open-source tool for creating polished screen demos and walkthrough videos. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/getopenscreen/openscreen) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: OpenScreen is a free, open-source desktop app for recording your screen and editing the footage into polished product demos and walkthrough videos, with a headless CLI for scripts and AI agents.
summary.what_it_does: Records a specific window or the whole screen, with microphone and system audio, plus an optional webcam picture-in-picture overlay. The timeline editor offers auto or manual zooms that follow the cursor, custom cursor size, smoothing and click effects, backgrounds, motion blur, crop, trim, and per-segment speed control. It adds text, arrow, and image annotations, and on-device automatic captions with an editable transcript. Export is to MP4 or GIF in several aspect ratios and resolutions, with GPU encoding (Metal, D3D11, Vulkan) and a CPU fallback. A CLI can record, edit `.openscreen` project JSON, and export headlessly, and an optional AI editing assistant can apply edits from chat using the user's own API key.
use_cases: Make a product demo video for social media or a landing page
Record a software walkthrough with zooms and captions
Create GIF demos for docs or posts
Automate screen recording and export in CI or scripts
Have an AI coding agent produce a video of a pull request change
Add subtitles and trim a screen recording
how_to_run: Windows: winget install --source msstore OpenScreen (or the .exe from GitHub Releases)
macOS: download the .dmg from the Releases page and drag OpenScreen to Applications
Linux: sudo apt install ./Openscreen-Linux-*.deb (or .rpm, .pacman, or .AppImage from Releases)
notable: Community continuation of Siddharth Vaddem's archived OpenScreen, under the same MIT license
Headless CLI with NDJSON output for scripts, CI, and AI coding agents
On-device automatic captions that work offline, with transcript-based cutting
Optional AI editing assistant with bring-your-own key for multiple providers; nothing enabled by default
Free for personal and commercial use
caveats: Under active development; expect rough edges and breaking changes to the project format and CLI
macOS 13+ required; macOS 15+ re-asks for screen-recording permission periodically
Windows .exe is unsigned and triggers SmartScreen; Linux system audio and cursor features depend on PipeWire and udev/input setup
keywords: record my screen for a tutorial
